(Betal Singh)
 Versus
 (The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
 Appearance:
 (By Shri Bhupendra Singh Rajput - Advocate)
 (By Shri Aps Tomar - Public Prosecutor)
 Order

This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant in connection with Crime No. 438 of 2023 registered at Police Station - Janakganj, District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.

First application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.11.2023 passed in M.CrC. No.40496/2023 with liberty to revive his prayer after recording of evidence of complainant or if the trial gets further delayed.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

It is further argued that in this case the evidence of complainants (PW-1) Munni &
(PW-2) Bhagwan Singh have been recorded.
Further argument is that aforesaid witnesses have come forward only after their warrant of arrest have been issued and they were arrested.
This shows the mala-fide of prosecution witnesses.

It is further argued that in the light of the evidence of (PW-1)
Munni from para 6 to 10 entire prosecution story becomes doubtful because the complainant denied having knowledge about the contents 2 MCRC-7121-2024 of complaint filed by her.
It is further argued that she has not indicted the name of present applicant/accused in her complaint.
Bhagwan Singh has also not supported the case of prosecution and turned hostile, in these circumstances, entire prosecution story becomes doubtful.
The applicant is in custody since 24.07.2023.
After conclusion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, further custodial interrogation is no more required.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Gwalior (M.P.) and there i s no possibility of his absconding or tempering with prosecution case.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its dismissal.

6.
